thread:
jess (eng-platform): spinning up a quick prototype for an "inflight request cost estimator" — idea is a live card in the console that shows estimated cost for requests currently being processed. wants to discuss attribution rules and perf impact.

matt (billing): love the idea. main ask: make sure it maps back to per-route and per-tenant chargebacks. if the estimator is noisy we could mis-bill. :eyes:

sana (eng-runtime): quick concerns: 1) estimator p99 cost calc needs current model SKU + quantization factor, 2) how do we account for cache hits that happen mid-request (prefix cache or KV hits)?

jess (eng-platform): sketching a formula in the proto: `estimated_cost = sum_over_tokens(model_price_per_token * token_count * quality_factor) - cache_credit`. cache_credit is tricky bc cache can be applied after request started.

matt (billing): can we surface both gross and net (post-cache) cost in the card? gross for quota checks, net for billing. separate fields.

sana (eng-runtime): agree — runtime can emit an "anticipated_cache_hit_rate" metric at request start. estimator can subtract a conservative credit. if we over-credit we risk undercharging. maybe show a range: `net_estimate = gross - [min_credit..max_credit]`

oliver (prod-analytics): for telemetry we need to log: route_id, tenant_id, model_sku, tokens_requested, tokens_returned, expected_cache_savings_pct, estimator_version. keeps a diffable trail. also sampling: do we send this for every request? that's a lot.

jess (eng-platform): plan: sample 1% by default, 10% for routes in "pilot" group, full for Dedicated customers. expose sampling rate in console.

matt (billing): sampling is ok if we have good extrapolation. need to ensure the estimator has deterministic seed so sampled traffic isn't biased. also want a way to recalc historical charges from raw logs when we turn sampling off.

sana (eng-runtime): implementation note: estimator will run in-path for the card (cheap arithmetic) and async for final reconciliation. runtime will emit post-run actuals that can reconcile the estimate. this keeps latency impact minimal.

jess (eng-platform): ui idea: live card shows three numbers: Gross tokens * unit price (est), Cache credit (est range), Net est. hover to expand to model/quantization assumptions. small CTA: "recompute from logs" to pull reconciled final values.

oliver (prod-analytics): important: include estimator_version and sampling_rate in logs so analytics can weight correctly. also tag records with `reconciled: true/false` once post-run reconciliation occurs.

ci-bot: deploy: started build `inflight-cost-estimator/v1` -> staging at `infra/staging` :green_heart:

sana (eng-runtime): note on cache-credit propagation: when KV/prefix cache evicts mid-request we currently attribute the earlier tokens as cache-miss and later tokens as cache-hit. estimator should follow same policy to avoid attribution jumps. check `cache/shim` behavior.

jess (eng-platform): open question: how to show SLO-aware adjustments? e.g., if route is latency-sensitive we may prefer to show gross cost to decide routing, while for billing we want net. any objections to two toggles: "show billing view" and "show routing view"?

matt (billing): that sounds right. also add "apply rounding policy" toggle for UI (monthly billing requires cents granularity).

oliver (prod-analytics): experiment suggestion: run estimator v1 alongside a control for 2 weeks, compare estimator_net vs reconciled_net, measure bias/variance, then decide sampling default. we can compute MAPE and false-billing rate.

jess (eng-platform): next steps: 1) sana to add anticipated_cache_hit_rate emission + reconciled post-run event (ticketed), 2) oliver to draft analytics evaluation pipeline, 3) matt to confirm billing rounding rules and tolerance, 4) i'll wire up the staging card + toggle mockups.

sana (eng-runtime): ack, i'll create a PR for the runtime metrics and add a small perf microbenchmark.

matt (billing): ack, will spam you with edgecases about rounding. :joy:

jess (eng-platform): thanks all — will push a staging build and post a short demo tomorrow. :thumbsup:
